# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**Governing Policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23**
**Member:** Morgan Foster
**Member ID:** W162894592
**Reference Number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
**Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), Illinois

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I am asking that the plan reconsider this denial in light of my medical records and the plan's own published criteria.

## Why I Believe My Records Meet the Plan's Criteria

The denial states that my request does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. I have reviewed Clinical Policy CP.MP.114, and I believe my records support each of the requirements the policy lists. Below, I have quoted the plan's own language and matched it to what is documented in my case.

**1. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc**

The policy states: "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

My MRI of the lumbar spine, performed 2026-06-26, found an L4-L5 disc extrusion.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging**

The policy states: "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

The same MRI documented "severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root."

**3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit**

The policy states: "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

My records document radicular pain radiating into my right calf, along with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level identified on imaging, and positive provocative testing on the affected side.

**4. Failed conservative therapy — physical therapy or home exercise program**

The policy states: "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate;"

I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17 (18 visits), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the four-week threshold in the policy.

**5. Failed conservative therapy — activity modification**

The policy states: "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;"

[Placeholder: documentation confirming ≥ four weeks of activity modification, or a note that this was addressed as part of the PT/home exercise program, to be added by my provider.] I am noting this because my records show I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes due to my symptoms, but I want to make sure the specific activity-modification documentation the plan is asking for is included in the file it reviews.

**6. Failed conservative therapy — NSAID or acetaminophen**

The policy states: "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

I used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, well beyond the three-week threshold.

**7. Failed conservative therapy — epidural steroid injection**

The policy states: "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

## Summary

Based on the records described above, I believe the documentation in my file addresses each of the criteria the plan's own policy lists for medical necessity: a diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc, nerve root compression confirmed by imaging, radiculopathy with a sensory deficit in a nerve root distribution, and conservative therapy consisting of physical therapy, NSAID use, and an epidural steroid injection, each exceeding the durations specified in the policy. I am asking the plan to confirm that the activity-modification documentation noted above is complete, and to reconsider the denial with the full record in view.

I am not a medical professional, and I am relying on my surgeon's clinical judgment that this surgery is necessary. I am asking the plan to take a full, fair look at the record already submitted, together with the additional documentation referenced above, and reverse this denial.

## Request

I respectfully request that this denial be reconsidered and that authorization for CPT 63030 be approved based on the records described above. If any additional documentation is needed from Dr. Reyes's office, please let me know as soon as possible so it can be submitted before the appeal deadline.

**This appeal must be received by 2027-02-19.**

**Submission:** Ambetter/Centene appeals are handled per state. Please go to ambetterhealth.com, select Illinois, and use the state's appeal or grievance form, or call the number on my member ID card. I am also mailing this appeal to the address printed on my denial notice, as that address is authoritative for my case.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Morgan Foster
Member ID: W162894592
Date: [insert date of submission]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Email: [insert email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee coverage.*
